questions.prompt: The pastebin has three validation layers. Explain what each layer is for and which one is authoritative.

keyPoints.text: The UI's disable-above-100,000-chars guard is a convenience for honest users, not a security boundary.
The request records' Validate() methods are the authoritative input boundary of the API.
Store-level invariants exist to protect what is persisted and what reads return, regardless of endpoint behavior.
The store enforces expiry both when a single paste is read and when an update is attempted.
Create requests validate content presence and size, enum definedness, and a minimum-length delete key, returning a field-to-errors dictionary.

questions.prompt: Explain the authorization model: who may edit or delete a paste, and why is this not authentication?

keyPoints.text: Edit and delete rights come from holding the delete key - a shared secret checked by hash.
keyPoints.quote: authorization by possession of a shared secret, not authentication

keyPoints.text: Presenting the right key proves nothing about who the caller is.
keyPoints.quote: It does not identify a user.

keyPoints.text: Slug routes expose resources directly, and read access is by design granted to anyone holding the link.
A classic junior mistake is to treat knowledge of a random slug as if it were a permission grant.
keyPoints.quote: Treating a random slug as permission.

keyPoints.text: Unlisted pastes must be kept out of the recent and search listings or the link-secrecy model collapses.
keyPoints.quote: Forgetting unlisted pastes must stay out of recent/search lists.

keyPoints.text: The actual hash comparison guards live in the store's update and delete methods.

questions.prompt: Threat-model DELETE /api/pastes/{slug}: what stops an attacker today, and which defenses are missing?

keyPoints.text: Start from an attacker who knows the slug but does not hold the key.
Their attack path is simply to submit guessed keys over and over.
The sole defense in place is the delete-key hash comparison.
keyPoints.quote: What stops them today? Hash check only.

keyPoints.text: Nothing throttles brute force anywhere in the request pipeline.
keyPoints.quote: Are brute-force attempts rate-limited? No rate limiting found.

keyPoints.text: The frontend also ships the delete key in the query string, where it can leak into logs and history.
Recommended hardening: move the secret into the body, add rate limiting, log without secret values, and cover it all with tests.
keyPoints.quote: Rate limiting, body-based secret, structured logging without secret values, tests.
